```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
raw <- readRDS('PLACES_FILTERED')
```

```{r}
meas_cols <- names(raw)[7:ncol(raw)]
data <- raw %>%
  group_by(loc_id) %>%
  summarise(
    across(c(TotalPopulation, TotalPop18plus, Geolocation), first),
    across(all_of(meas_cols), function(x) first(x[!is.na(x)])),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) # this just groups all the loc_ids and combines rows

us <- filter(data, loc_id == "US--59") 
# apparently there's a US avg row idfk, just set it aside for now 

data <- data %>% filter(loc_id != "US--59")
colSums(is.na(data[meas_cols]))       
dim(data)
table(rowSums(!is.na(data[meas_cols])))

data[rowSums(!is.na(data[meas_cols])) == 0, c("loc_id")]

```

- compressed the dataset into one unique row per county, there is one county without any data: Loving TX. Removed the confidence interval for eda specifically

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
for (i in c("Obesity among adults", "Diagnosed diabetes among adults",
            "Current cigarette smoking among adults", "Depression among adults",
            "High blood pressure among adults", "Any disability among adults")) {
  hist(data[[i]], breaks = 30, col = "thistle", border = "steelblue", main = i)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

par(mar = c(12, 4, 2, 1))
boxplot(data[meas_cols], names = meas_cols, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.6, col = "thistle")
par(mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2))
```

- used bar graph to plot all 35, below is code to do that but with histograms, 

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(3, 4), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1)) 
for (i in meas_cols){
  hist(data[[i]], breaks = 30, col = "thistle", border = "steelblue", main = i, cex.main = 0.7)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2))     
```

- idk heres some more plots glhf

```{r}
short <- setNames(sub(" among adults.*$", "", meas_cols), meas_cols)
cors <- cor(data[meas_cols], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
dimnames(cors) <- list(short[meas_cols], short[meas_cols])
```

```{r, fig.width=11, fig.height=10}
as.data.frame(as.table(cors)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Var1, Var2, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = 'red', mid = 'white', high = 'steelblue') +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(fill = "r")
```

```{r}
as.data.frame(as.table(cors)) %>%
  rename(m1 = Var1, m2 = Var2, r = Freq) %>%
  filter(as.character(m1) < as.character(m2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(r))) %>%
  head(15)
```

- top correlations ranked
